answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with basalt ballast: a new agent stakes 30 POA, locked 28 days, then rides six chained tasks, each next task appearing only after the last is verified, with deadlines drawn from a random ocean schedule of two to thirty-six hours, so farms must staff operators around the clock. Three gale auditors across time zones re-run one task each; any mismatch burns 10 POA. Trust decays five percent per idle epoch, so bought accounts rot. Forging 100 agents locks 3,000 POA and costs $8,400 in wages. Like ballast, the stake holds only while the ship keeps sailing.
